## Highlights

- Projects can run separate task workers for the same agent, wake a standing
  coordinator when capacity becomes available, and review a declared batch of up
  to twenty captured targets. Each review still requires independent evidence.
  The Tale CLI can provision pristine operational review contexts and manage agent
  model selections alongside the project's other configuration.
  [#4603](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4603),
  [#4608](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4608),
  [#4616](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4616),
  [#4632](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4632)
- Automation transforms have their own analysis budget, allowing bodies of up to
  16,384 UTF-16 code units and 4,096 tokens. Ordinary expressions keep their
  smaller limits. The CLI compiler and runtime validator enforce the same bounds.
  [#4639](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4639)
- A delayed failure while reading an organization's default provider credentials
  no longer removes a newer cached read. Changing the defaults still invalidates
  that organization's cache; credentials remain scoped to the organization.
  [#4641](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4641)
- Maintainers can finish cancelled validation graphs across all seven supported
  CI workflows when their substantive jobs have ended and only unallocated
  summary jobs remain. Source, queue and job checks still refuse active work;
  cancellation never counts as successful validation.
  [#4638](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4638)
- Sandbox commands no longer inherit the runtime daemon's token. The daemon
  retains it for its authenticated API.
  [#4635](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4635)

- `tale deploy observe` reports retained deployment identity, configuration and
  runtime diagnostics without applying changes. Its evidence is read-only
  observation; it does not certify deployment acceptance or readiness.

## Upgrade notes

- v0.5.78, v0.5.79 and v0.5.80 were stopped before complete release publication.
  Preserve their existing tags, package snapshots and any architecture images;
  do not rebuild or retag them. This forward release includes their source changes.
  The retained [v0.5.80 notes](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/blob/63c7499137c84f7828f30472dc908a993622e48b/.github/release-notes/v0.5.80.md)
  describe those features and their inherited upgrade requirements; they are not
  evidence that those versions finished deploying.
- Back up the application and knowledge databases, configuration, keys and
  external stores. Follow the supported legacy runtime bridge and confirm zero
  unfinished legacy automation runs before managed protocol-2 cutover. Apply the
  complete ordered migration inventory, retain execution holds and reserve the
  vector-copy disk headroom described in the
  [v0.5.79 upgrade requirements](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/blob/0ee5fd9656dc12f08976155d956ee76fe39f4ea3/.github/release-notes/v0.5.79.md#upgrade-notes).
  Do not roll back by manually starting an older image.
- Upgrade the CLI and runtime together before applying configurations containing
  larger transform bodies or managed review contexts. A configuration-only update
  cannot install the parser, worker or migration changes. A deployment that must
  cross the legacy bridge can preserve its installed packs with an explicitly
  empty configuration selection; verify the retained identities before and after
  that bridge, then apply the new packs with the compatible runtime.
- Enable coordinator wakes explicitly with `wakeOnSlotFreed: true` through the
  Tale CLI. Only one schedule may claim a project's wake. Review contexts must be
  pristine operational tasks, and each captured target still requires a matching
  independent decision. Agent definitions, model selections and review contexts
  grant no credentials and do not guarantee twenty concurrent workers; provider,
  organization and host limits still govern admission.
- Retain the v0.5.80 guidance for API contract `3.27.0`, MCP clients, newly counted
  usage dimensions and private-route deployment acceptance. Finish the runtime
  rollout before relying on uniform behavior across processes.
